findings.finding: The cooling appliance meaning is distinct from the distilling condenser. The derivation explicitly relates refrigerate and the agent/instrument -or suffix. This supports a modern refrigerate plus -or candidate with its exact authored spelling.

The protective state and precautions are distinguished from financial collateral and securities. The origin links secure and -ity while recording borrowing through Latin; a current morphological relation must not be presented as an English historical coinage.

Separate headwords distinguish coating or incrustation, a weighing instrument, and gradations or proportional measurement. Their histories also differ. An existing shared spelling identity cannot by itself establish interchangeable parts for weighing scale, limescale and drawing or assessment scales.

The selected lifting-device sense is distinguished from the electrical socket, playing card, personal name and other meanings. No person-name or diminutive segmentation is justified for the modern pallet-handling component.

The goods-support platform is a separate headword from the straw bed. Its borrowed history does not justify English pal plus -let segmentation. The modern platform can remain a whole part in pallet and pallet jack.
The selected appliance keeps contents frozen. The derivation explicitly relates freeze and -er. No source temperature or food-handling procedure is copied into the lesson.

The attached information-bearing material and the verb of applying it are related uses; descriptive categories and computing labels are separately described. The borrowed modern label stem need not be split by its letters.
The literal noun is an attached indication of an item's price, distinct from the extended cost reading. Price plus tag can preserve the literal compound and its space.
The suffix forms abstract state, condition and quality nouns. This supports the proposed secure/security relationship at an explicit modern teaching depth, subject to exact Growth-family inspection.

The headword denotes a manually propelled small truck and points to the wheeled frame sense. Automatically collected violent news examples are not lesson evidence. Dictionary.com's hand-truck page was also retrieved but its unqualified truck cross-reference alone was insufficient.

The wheeled transport noun includes the handled upright frame, other small platforms and road-hauling vehicles. The barter noun/verb is a different family. Shared morphological family membership does not make those completed lexical senses synonyms.
